data.title: FSSAI prohibits sale of 'unsafe, substandard' Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener, company responds
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has directed an immediate ban on sale of Nestle India's "low-fat dairy whitener". The food regulator called the product "unsafe and substandard" on Saturday.

A sample of "low-fat dairy whitener" manufactured by Nestle India has failed the safety test conducted by FSSAI. FSSAI said that the sample, which was collected from the premises of Hotel Lalit in Connaught Place, New Delhi, has been found "unsafe and substandard".

Nestle denied the allegations and said, "Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements. Phosphorus is a nutrient that occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in all milk-based products."

"FSSAI lab reports reflect total phosphorus against the additive limit, without accounting for the substantial natural phosphorus contribution from milk-based ingredients. Our product is in full compliance for added phosphorus as per prescribed limits under FSSR including for as consumed basis. We have been in continuous engagement with the authorities as per due process established under law and have shared data across other same/similar milk-based products in the category to reflect presence of naturally occurring phosphorous." the statement from Nestle read.

Via a post on X, FSSAI said that the product was found "substandard" and "unsafe" as per the report of the food analyst's laboratory, violating the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.

The regulator added that a copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator (FBO) for reference and necessary action.

A notice has been sent to Bharat Hotels Ltd over the product and its non-compliance.

Under the relevant section of the FSS Act, 2006, the FBO was eligible to appeal against the food analyst's report within a prescribed time period.

FSSAI has now directed the FBO to immediately stop the sale of the identified food product.

"A sample of Nestle "Low Fat Dairy Whitener" collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd. (The Lalit), New Delhi, has been declared UNSAFE & SUBSTANDARD by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act 2006," read the post on social media.

Previously, FSSAI had flagged Nestle India's infant nutrition products. The food regulator initiated legal action against Nestle India Ltd in three cases over alleged promotional violations and nutritional non-compliance in its infant food portfolio.

The legal proceedings involved promotional claims for two infant formula brands, NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1, as well as a follow-up formula sample that didn't meet prescribed nutritional parameters in laboratory tests.

"In NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, claims relating to '5 HMOs' and 'Whey Protein' were observed, while in Lactogen Pro 1, a claim relating to 'Whey Protein' being easy to digest was observed. Accordingly, clarifications were sought from M/s Nestle India Limited regarding the above claims," FSSAI said.

"Both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the FSS (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020, which restricts promotional claims/material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods, and Section 3 of the IMS Act, 1992, which prohibits their advertisement and promotion," FSSAI added.

However, Nestle India had maintained that it remains compliant with all applicable regulations in India.

data.title: Review of Sony BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7, Sub 8, Rear 8
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- I want to start by saying that you can actually enjoy movies best at the cinema, but you cannot easily replicate that experience or have it when it comes to shows/series at home. This is where having a good sound system adds a lot of stuff. It completely redefines the viewing experience. Entertainment cannot be just visuals only.

Sound adds the real depth, the feel, the essence, and without it, you are only receiving half the artistic intent of a scene.

To truly understand the value of what sound is all about, I want you to look beyond the basic acoustic limitations of modern televisions.

Today's displays are remarkably thin, which leaves absolutely no physical cabinet space for speaker drivers to move air. The result is a flat, lifeless acoustic signature. I have been testing a modular trio from Sony for quite some time, claiming to solve this problem.

This trio system consists of the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7 (Rs 99,990) handling the front and height channels, the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 (Rs 42,990) delivering the low-frequency rumble, and the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers (Rs 42,990) wrapping the room in immersive surround sound. Let me tell you all about my experience when I combined them to find out if this trio system is the best home theater setup that you can have.

BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7:

The centerpiece of this entire system is the BRAVIA Theatre Bar 7. Visually, it is a sleek, low-profile soundbar wrapped in an acoustic fabric that slips seamlessly under your television. But inside the chassis, it is an engineered powerhouse. The Bar 7 packs nine dedicated speaker units, including side-firing drivers and up-firing units designed to physically bounce height channels off your ceiling.

From an audiophile standpoint, what the Bar 7 does flawlessly is anchor the vocal clarity. Credit to its dedicated center channel processing, dialogues are crisp and well-separated from the chaotic background noise of an action sequence. It supports the heavy-hitting spatial formats like Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, and is even IMAX Enhanced.

However, if there is one caveat to the Bar 7 as a standalone unit, it is the lower frequency response. It delivers crystal-clear mids and highs, but because of its compact volume, it simply does not get low or loud enough on its own to provide a truly cinematic punch. I guess that's exactly why it requires the rest of the trio.

BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8:

This is where the BRAVIA Theatre Sub 8 comes into play, and it completely transforms the acoustic signature of the system. A soundbar handles the intricate directional details, but a dedicated subwoofer is what gives the audio its physical weight and presence.

Armed with a 300W amplifier and a large 200mm driver unit, the Sub 8 handles the heavy lifting for the low-end frequencies. In the audio world, a good sub doesn't just make noise; it moves air.

You stop just hearing an explosion on screen and start actually feeling the shockwave reverberate through the floorboards. What impressed me the most is how well the crossover is managed. The Sub 8 delivers propulsive, controlled bass that grounds the action sequences without ever muddying the mid-range or overpowering the vocals coming from the Bar 7.

BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8:

As pristine as the front stage and bass are, the system achieves true immersiveness when you add the BRAVIA Theatre Rear 8 wireless speakers. These two speakers add the 5.1 kind of depth that you absolutely need. When you install them and set them up behind the backside of where you sit, that placement makes things profoundly immersive.

It is here that Sony's 360 'Spatial Sound Mapping' goes into overdrive. The system does not just passively push sound to the back of the room; it mathematically generates multiple 'phantom speakers' in a dome around and above you.

When a helicopter flies past on the screen, you genuinely hear the rotors move seamlessly from the front Bar 7, across the ceiling, and fade into the Rear 8s behind you. All of a sudden, I started to feel as if I am genuinely watching a movie in a premium commercial theater. They elevate the soundstage from a flat, two-dimensional plane to a living, breathing environment.

The Setup Experience:

This Sony trio is easily the easiest setup I have ever experienced. You simply place the units in their respective spots, plug them into a power outlet, and open the smartphone app.

The BRAVIA Connect app takes care of everything. There is no complicated calibration microphone to wave around the room. The system uses 'Sound Field Optimization', sending out a quick pulse of sound to digitally map your specific room's acoustic characteristics. Within seconds, it calibrates the sound field height and optimizes the spatial mapping for your exact seating position. And if you are an enthusiast who wants to tinker, the app allows for pro-level customizations, letting you adjust the sound field, voice modes, and individual rear speaker levels to perfectly match your preferences.

Non-5.1 Content:

At times, if the content is not natively 5.1 or Dolby Atmos ready, the system can struggle slightly with the upmixing. When you are watching standard stereo broadcasts or compressed streaming video, the audio can become very heavy when the sound goes up. Because Sony's upmixing algorithm is aggressive in trying to utilize all the physical and phantom speakers, standard flat audio is pushed hard into the surround channels.

This can make the background score or ambient noise feel dense and overwhelming in the lower frequencies. Thankfully, it is quite normal when the vocals are active; dialogue never gets lost. But the balance you hear on a 4K Blu-ray can occasionally feel a bit artificially inflated on basic content.

In The End:

If you are planning to invest in this setup, here is my practical take on getting the best out of it. First, running the Sound Field Optimization in the BRAVIA Connect app is non-negotiable; skipping it leaves the spatial audio flat, whereas running it properly maps the phantom speakers to your ceiling height and room dimensions.

Second, definitely make use of the app's 'Voice Mode' for poorly mixed movies where action effects tend to drown out dialogues, it isolates speech cleanly without distorting the rest of the mix. I think, buying the Bar 7 without the Sub 8 is an incomplete experience, so go for the trio to bring in a sense of authority that true home cinema demands.

For a few of you, I do not expect this trio to double as a dedicated audiophile Hi-Fi setup for stereo music streaming. And the reason is simple. In my opinion, this trio is tuned specifically for cinematic theatricality, where standard music tracks can occasionally feel a bit clinical or bass-heavy. If you're an enthusiast then do note that there are no manual multiband EQ controls (you rely on Sony's automated Sound Field profiles).

Then there is no alphanumeric LED display on the front grille, so you have to glance at the TV or phone app just to check volume levels and active codecs. Last but not least, there are occasional momentary audio dropouts over HDMI during dead-silent scenes where the bar momentarily sleeps and clips the very first syllable when audio resumes.

Despite that minor quirk with standard audio, Sony has proved their mettle in terms of what they have done with this ecosystem. The combination of the Bar 7, Sub 8, and Rear 8 delivers an expansive, surreal soundstage that redefines home entertainment. So yes, it is simply one of the best.

My Rating: 4/5

data.title: 5 public sector banks post 15-25% credit growth in Q2FY27
data.description:
Public sector banks (PSBs) seem to have done fairly well on credit growth in the second quarter (Q2) of FY27, posting year-on-year (yoy) growth in the 15-25 per cent range, even as the gap between credit growth and deposit growth persists.

Deposit growth has ranged from 7 per cent to 14 per cent yoy, lagging credit growth, according to provisional business figures disclosed by five PSBs so far.

As per RBI’s latest data (August) on sectoral deployment of bank credit, the demand has been higher vis-a-vis the year-ago period across all four segments -- agriculture and allied activities, industry, services and personal loans.

PNB’s advances grow 14.8 per cent

Punjab National Bank (PNB) reported a 14.8 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 9.9 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹13,42,693 crore and ₹17,77,097 crore, respectively.

Within gross advances and total deposits, PNB’s domestic advances and domestic deposits were up 12.59 per cent yoy (to stand at ₹12,58,583 crore as at September-end 2026) and 9.44 per cent yoy (to ₹17,11,696 crore), respectively.

As at September-end 2026, the gap between domestic credit and advances growth stood at 315 basis points. One basis point equals one-hundredth of a percentage point.

Union Bank sees 18.53 per cent growth

Union Bank of India (UBI) clocked an 18.53 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 6.87 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹11,55,930 crore and ₹13,19,457 crore, respectively.

Within gross advances and total deposits, UBI’s domestic advances and domestic deposits were up 17.36 per cent yoy (to stand at ₹11,05,807 crore as at September-end 2026) and 6.88 per cent yoy (to ₹13,18,977 crore), respectively. As at September-end 2026, the gap between domestic credit and advances growth stood at 1,048 basis points.

The share of RAM (Retail, Agriculture and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprise) advances in UBI’s domestic advances declined to 57.47 per cent as at September-end 2026, from 58.82 per cent as at September-end 2025.

The proportion of CASA (Current Account, Savings Account) deposits in UBI’s domestic deposits improved to 34.93 per cent as at September-end 2026, up from 32.56 per cent as at September-end 2025.

Indian Bank reports 16.6 per cent growth

Indian Bank reported a 16.6 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 12.4 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹7.23 lakh crore and ₹8.73 lakh crore, respectively.

The share of CASA deposits in Indian Bank’s domestic deposits improved to 39.28 per cent as at September-end 2026, up from 38.87 per cent as at September-end 2025.

UCO Bank, P&SB post double-digit growth

UCO Bank recorded a 24.68 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 14.05 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹2.88 lakh crore and ₹3.49 lakh crore, respectively.

Punjab & Sind Bank reported a 19.37 per cent yoy growth in gross advances and 12.98 per cent growth in total deposits. As at September-end 2026, the bank’s gross advances and total deposits stood at ₹1,26,011 crore and ₹1,53,317 crore, respectively.

data.title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed execution
data.description:
By Sheila Dang

The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection.

The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers wrote in a Friday court filing. It is the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to halt attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026.

Lee said on Saturday that Frank Strada has resigned as Department of Correction commissioner and would leave his position this month. The governor had ordered an independent review of the execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital.

Strada, in a separate statement, said that although he believes his agency's personnel followed proper protocol, "stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward."

An interim commissioner will be announced later, the governor's office said.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment,” Lee said in a statement.

Pike's lawyers have accused Correction Department officials of ignoring prior warnings from her doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis would make placing intravenous lines especially difficult.

Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995, when Pike was 18.

Doctors were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her lawyers said on Friday.

data.title: BlackRock's IBIT ETF Flashes Golden Cross As SEC Approves Triple-Leveraged Bitcoin, Ethereum ETPs
data.description:
Key points:
  • BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF has its 50-day average moving above its 200-day average.
  • The SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change on Friday to allow listing of six 3x leveraged products from Volatility Shares’ VS Trust.
  • Trading in each fund can only begin once the fund's registration has become effective.

BlackRock’s (BLK) iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) flashed a golden cross on Saturday, as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved a rule change to allow triple-leveraged Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) products to be listed.

According to Koyfin data, IBIT’s 50-day simple moving average (SMA) was 41.97, only up from its 200-day average of 41.92. The shorter average crosses above the longer one to form a golden cross. Traders often read it as a bullish sign.

SoSoValue data showed US spot Bitcoin (BTC) exchange-traded funds began October with new inflows. The funds had net inflows of $102.67 million on Oct. 1. Topping the list was BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF with $195.57 million.

IBIT’s inflow exceeded the group’s net inflow. SoSoValue data showed total net assets across the funds hit $109.34 billion. Net inflows through October 1 for the week to date were $51.25 million

Leveraged Bitcoin, Ethereum Funds Approved

In addition to the daily flows, the SEC implemented an action that could broaden the selection of Bitcoin products.

The SEC approved a Cboe BZX Exchange rule change on Friday, according to a filing. It allows six of the products from Volatility Shares’ VS Trust to list on the exchange. Each seeks three times the daily return of its benchmark. The lineup includes Bitcoin and Ethereum (ETH) as well as gold, silver, crude oil and natural gas.

Volatility Shares has previously filed for leveraged crypto funds. In its 2023 filing for the 2x Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITX), the firm said such funds seek to achieve a set multiple of daily returns. It also pointed out that returns over longer periods can diverge from that multiple and can even move in the reverse direction. The new products put leveraged crypto alongside commodity funds.

No trading in any fund shall occur before the fund's registration becomes effective, and no trading date will be set.

Bitcoin’s price was trading around $84,800, down over 0.2% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC dropped to ‘bearish’ from the ‘neutral’ zone, as chatter rose to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels over the past day.

data.title: "Unique programme": CM Naidu highlights IIT alumni network at PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026
data.description:
Vijayawada, Oct. 3 -- Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday described the PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026 as a unique initiative and highlighted the potential of leveraging the knowledge and expertise of IIT alumni to help develop the state into a global knowledge hub.

Speaking to ANI, Naidu said, "This is a unique program. India has 5 lakh IIT alumni. If you see these alumni, if you use that knowledge, we can do wonders. That is why, for the first time, they are establishing the World Amaravati IITians Council. They are going to give ideas continuously, subject-wise. They are going to involve universities, all IITs, to work together. This is where knowledge will be exchanged, and we will prepare for tomorrow. Ultimately, Andhra Pradesh is going to benefit by becoming a global knowledge hub."

The maiden PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026, organised by PanIIT Alumni India in collaboration with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, brought together IIT leaders, policymakers, industry leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, academicians, technology experts and innovators to discuss a long-term technology and innovation roadmap for Andhra Pradesh.

According to an official release, the summit was formally inaugurated by Nara Lokesh, Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, Government of Andhra Pradesh, with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by Katamneni, IAS, Secretary, Department of ITE&C, Government of Andhra Pradesh; KN Satyanarayana, Director, IIT Tirupati; V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras; Anand Kumar, MD, STMicroelectronics India; and Mall.

He was joined by Swadeep Pillarisetti, Chair, PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026; Amitabh Ranjan, Vice Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India; Prabhat Kumar, IRS, Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India; Bhaskar Katamneni, IAS, Secretary, Department of ITE&C, Government of Andhra Pradesh; KN Satyanarayana, Director, IIT Tirupati; V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras; Anand Kumar, MD, STMicroelectronics India; and Mallik Tatipamula, CTO, Ericsson Silicon Valley.

Held at Dr BR Ambedkar Kala Vedika, Vijayawada, the Summit was themed "Andhra's Resilient DeepTech Decade: Anchored by PanIIT- Swarna Andhra to Viksit Bharat 2047." The Summit sought to connect the collective strength of the 23 IITs and the global 5-lakh-plus IIT alumni network with Andhra Pradesh's development priorities.

The day-long Summit featured intensive discussions on some of the most critical technology and development priorities.

The sessions covered Energy in the Age of AI; DeepTech in All Walks of Life and Product Perfection; Space, Aerospace & Defence Manufacturing; Bio Valley- Health Access & Screening at Scale; and AgriTech- Farmers & Water Security.

The discussions brought together senior representatives from government, IITs, global technology companies, industry and startups, including experts from IBM, NXP Semiconductors, Ericsson, AWS, Honeywell Aerospace, Apollo Hospitals, ICMR, ICRISAT and leading Indian technology and manufacturing companies.

The Summit also featured fireside conversations on Skilling & Entrepreneurship and AI in Governance, besides a presentation on Amaravati Capital City.

The Valedictory Session presented a series of institutional initiatives designed to create sustained engagement between PanIIT, the IIT ecosystem, the Andhra Pradesh Government and industry.

PanIIT Amaravati Council, a proposed permanent platform and secretariat in Amaravati to connect the global IIT alumni network with Andhra Pradesh's long-term development agenda.

PanIIT Amaravati Venture Fund, a DeepTech investment mechanism aimed at supporting entrepreneurship and high-potential ventures in the State.

Global IIT Mentor Network, a proposed 100-member network to connect entrepreneurs, startups and young talent in Andhra Pradesh with experienced IIT alumni globally.

Industry Chairs, 10 proposed industry-linked chairs to strengthen research and industry-academia collaboration.

IIT Technology Transfer Pipeline, an initiative to identify and facilitate the commercialisation of technologies emerging from IITs.

DeepTech Policy Package, a proposed policy framework covering areas including AI, quantum technologies, semiconductors, energy, space, defence, healthcare, AgriTech and skilling.

The official Summit framework also identifies these initiatives as part of a longer-term PanIIT-Andhra Pradesh engagement.

One of the key moments of the Summit was the launch of Q-Shiva, involving five quantum computers, positioning quantum technology among the frontier areas being explored for Andhra Pradesh's emerging DeepTech ecosystem.

The programme also featured a demonstration by the Qubit Force team and the launch of the book "Quantum Children."

The Summit's discussions extended across Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, DeepTech, Quantum Computing, Semiconductors and Data Centres, MedTech and Healthcare, Oil & Gas and Green Energy, Space and Aerospace, Defence and AgriTech.

Three strategic roundtables were conducted in parallel, bringing together IIT Directors, venture capitalists and family offices, and industry leaders and unicorn CXOs. The roundtables focused on converting the Summit's ideas into partnerships, investments and institutional initiatives.

The Summit also included a technology exhibition and networking sessions connecting startups, investors, industry and the IIT ecosystem. It has about 50 stalls.

Prabhat Kumar, IRS, Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India, said that the Summit represents an opportunity to channel the collective strength of IIT alumni towards institution-building, innovation and nation-building.

Amitabh Ranjan, Vice Chairman, PanIIT Alumni India, said the objective was to create institutions and networks that would continue to work beyond the Summit, including a Council, venture fund, fellowship and mentor network.

Swadeep Pillarisetti, Chair, PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026, and Shri Sudhakar Gande, Chair/leadership representatives associated with the Summit, were among those who contributed to the initiative.

PanIIT Alumni India is the umbrella organisation representing alumni of all 23 Indian Institutes of Technology, with a global community of more than 500,000 alumni. Its objective is to channel the collective expertise, networks and resources of the IIT alumni community towards innovation, entrepreneurship, technology transfer and nation-building.

The PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026 concluded with the presentation of the PanIIT Amaravati initiatives, the Andhra PanIIT Declaration, the Q-Shiva launch and a roadmap for continued collaboration.

The Summit is positioned as the beginning of a longer-term engagement linking IIT talent, research, technology, entrepreneurship, capital and industry with Andhra Pradesh's development priorities.

The objective is clear: to build partnerships that move DeepTech from ideas and laboratories to products, enterprises and solutions contributing to Andhra Pradesh's journey towards Swarna Andhra 2047 and India's Viksit Bharat 2047.

data.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities this week, three sources say
  • Two sources say Khader is cooperating with FBI to identify fellow ShinyHunters hackers
  • Reuters analysis finds stolen data includes FBI employees' medical, psychiatric and personal information

By Jana Winter, Raphael Satter and AJ Vicens

A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Saif al-Din Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities, the three sources said. Two of them said he was brought into custody on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the circumstances of Khader’s detention or where he is being held. Two sources said that he is helping the FBI and global law enforcement locate the other hackers in the group.

The FBI declined to comment on any specific arrest or activity abroad but said that the bureau "continues to aggressively investigate the recent cyber incident allegedly involving ShinyHunters, having already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects — and we will spare no resource in bringing each of the responsible individuals to justice."

Reuters’ attempts to reach Khader and members of his family over the past week and a half have been unsuccessful.

The detention of Khader — whose alleged hacker nickname is Rey — is the latest twist in the case of ShinyHunters. The prolific cyber extortion group, which has a long history of targeting major corporations around the world, is believed by experts to consist mainly of young, English-speaking hackers focused on data theft and extortion.

Their theft of what they claim are mountains of data on every single FBI employee has drawn comparisons to the allegedly Chinese-linked intrusion at the US Office of Personnel Management in 2015, which compromised sensitive details on millions of Americans who had been vetted for security clearances.

SENSITIVE INFORMATION

A Reuters analysis of a sample of the data shared by ShinyHunters revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information of FBI employees, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information.

Khader's cooperation with investigators could be critical to helping contain — or at least understand — the damage. One source said he was walking investigators through his electronic devices and digital correspondence to help the FBI locate his cohorts.

"His cooperation is critical to ongoing efforts to arrest these hackers," the source told Reuters.

There have been hints for days that ShinyHunters was experiencing disruption following the announcement of its break-in at the FBI. Beginning on Tuesday, Reuters was unable to reach ShinyHunters through the online account it previously used to communicate with journalists. Then, on Wednesday, the group’s dark web site, where it had previously posted threats to the FBI, disappeared.

FBI Director Kash Patel had been hinting at more arrests following the announcement that another alleged ShinyHunters member, Pepijn van der Stap, had been detained in the Netherlands.

“FBI teams are working new leads RIGHT NOW,” Patel said on Wednesday in a message posted to X. “More arrests are on the table.”

The operators of a ShinyHunters-linked email address did not respond to a request for comment on Friday. The operators of that email account previously told Reuters that the group’s site had gone offline due to sabotage from rivals and "disruption due to an unrelated incident."

The group had previously struck a defiant note, saying on September 22 that it had hacked the FBI in retaliation over an advisory that accused ShinyHunters of making "exaggerated claims of access" to extort victims for money. It gave the FBI a week to withdraw the advisory.

But in the most recent email to Reuters, the operators struck a conciliatory tone, saying that “we want no further escalation” with the FBI. The operators said Reuters could interpret their message as meaning, “ShinyHunters backing down completely.”

KHADER'S IDENTITY LONG KNOWN

Khader’s identity, and his alleged connection to ShinyHunters, have long been known to security researchers.

Last year, the independent journalist Brian Krebs reported that Khader was a key member of Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters, an umbrella group of hackers that included ShinyHunters. Krebs, who said he spoke to Khader over Signal, quoted the teenager as saying he had quit the world of data breaches and extortion and was cooperating with law enforcement.

But ShinyHunters continued its hacking spree into 2026, claiming credit for break-ins at video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion involving education tool Canvas that ⁠caused widespread ​disruption across US schools.

Law enforcement agencies around the world, including in the United States, have struggled to arrest and prosecute members of related groups such as Lapsus$ or Scattered Spider, Reuters has previously reported.

Sources told Reuters that the difficulty stems from the hackers’ young ages, which can make prosecutions complex, or because the groups they belong to are so chaotic and informal, or because victims of their extortion attempts often decline to help investigators.

data.title: Retirement savings with an equity edge
data.description:
Retirement funds offered by mutual funds have recently seen a regulatory shake-up. There are 29 such schemes under the solution-oriented category, managing over ₹33,400 crore.

In February 2026, SEBI announced the discontinuation of solution-oriented schemes, including retirement and children’s funds, and introduced Life Cycle Funds as a new category. In March, however, it revised the framework and allowed fund houses to retain their existing retirement and children’s funds, subject to restrictions on launching Life Cycle Funds of certain tenures.

Consequently, AMCs retaining their retirement funds can launch only four Life Cycle Fund variants, compared with the maximum six otherwise permitted. Following this relaxation, almost all fund houses chose to retain their existing retirement schemes.

Retirement funds are open-ended schemes designed to build long-term wealth for investors after retirement. They allow fund managers to vary equity and debt exposure within specified limits. AMCs can offer up to four variants based on asset allocation, equity, aggressive hybrid, conservative hybrid and pure debt. For instance, HDFC Mutual Fund offers three variants, while ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund offers all four. These schemes generally have a mandatory lock-in period of five years or until the investor turns 60, whichever is earlier.

However, only a handful qualify for tax benefits under Section 80C. This allows eligible investments of up to ₹1.5 lakh a year to be deducted from taxable income under the old tax regime.

Among these schemes, ICICI Prudential Retirement Fund – Hybrid Aggressive Plan has been one of the better performers. Similar to aggressive hybrid funds, it allocates around 80 per cent of its portfolio to equities, with the balance invested in debt. It has outperformed several retirement schemes with similar mandates as well as the aggressive hybrid fund category.

Since its launch in February 2019, the fund has delivered a CAGR of 14 per cent. However, it does not qualify for tax benefits under Section 80C. As of August 2026, the fund managed assets worth ₹1,321 crore.

Asset allocation framework

The fund uses an in-house equity valuation model incorporating P/E, price-to-book value (P/BV) and other valuation parameters to determine its equity exposure.

It raises equity allocation when valuations and market conditions are favourable and turns more cautious when risks rise.

In line with its aggressive hybrid mandate, it maintains equity exposure in the 75-85 per cent range.

Equity strategy

The fund follows a bottom-up, market-cap and sector-agnostic stock selection approach, focusing on companies approaching an earnings turnaround.

It looks for businesses where much of the negative sentiment is already priced in and earnings are expected to improve over the next few quarters. The strategy is to identify such opportunities early and hold the stocks as long as earnings momentum persists.

Stock selection is driven primarily by earnings prospects and revisions. The fund looks for companies whose earnings potential is underappreciated by the market, as well as businesses poised for strong growth on favourable business-cycle trends. Valuations are assessed based on the potential for re-rating or de-rating rather than absolute P/E multiples. As per the latest portfolio, the top 10 equity holdings accounted for about 23 per cent of the fund’s overall assets.

Market-cap allocation is an outcome of stock selection rather than a predetermined target. Over the past five years, the fund has allocated an average 48 per cent of its total assets to large-cap stocks, 16 per cent to mid-caps and 13 per cent to small-caps. Currently, mid- and small-cap exposure stands at 19 per cent and 18 per cent, respectively, reflecting the fund manager’s assessment of better earnings opportunities in these segments. With nearly 80 per cent of its portfolio invested in equities, the fund is exposed to market volatility. Its significant allocation to mid- and small-cap stocks further increases the risk, particularly during market corrections.

The fund is currently overweight on banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), capital goods, and metals and mining, while underweight on information technology and consumer staples. Banks, retailing and industrial products are its three largest sector exposures. Over the past year, it has increased allocation to banks, insurance and healthcare services, while reducing exposure to transport services, finance, and cement and cement products.

Debt strategy

On the debt side, the fund invests across permissible debt instruments including government securities, corporate debt and money market instruments. Given its aggressive hybrid mandate and the scheme’s lock-in period, the fund is comfortable taking relatively higher duration exposure.

Over the past five years, the fund’s Macaulay duration has ranged from 0.3 to 4.9 years. As of August 2026, it stood at 2.9 years, with a portfolio yield to maturity (YTM) of 6.8 per cent. The portfolio had 4 per cent exposure to government securities, 2.7 per cent to AAA-rated and 3.7 per cent to AA-rated assets. It also held about 1 per cent in REITs and 7 per cent in cash equivalents.

Performance

Over the past seven years, the fund’s five-year rolling returns averaged 18 per cent CAGR, compared with 14 per cent for the average of six other retirement schemes with similar investment mandates. The aggressive hybrid fund category averaged 15 per cent over the same period. The fund’s five-year rolling returns ranged from 12.8 per cent to 24.4 per cent during this period.

On a three-year rolling-return basis, the fund delivered an average CAGR of 19 per cent, compared with 14 per cent for its relevant peers.

The fund’s annualised standard deviation, a measure of volatility, stood at 16.6 per cent, higher than the aggressive hybrid fund category average of 13.5 per cent.

The regular plan has a base expense ratio of 1.85 per cent, lower than the category average of 1.92 per cent. The direct plan’s expense ratio is 0.72 per cent, also below the category average of 0.87 per cent.

Unlike aggressive hybrid funds, retirement funds have a mandatory lock-in, which can help investors maintain discipline and avoid premature withdrawals. However, this comes at the cost of liquidity, and the scheme does not offer Section 80C tax benefits. It is, therefore, more suitable for investors specifically earmarking investments for retirement rather than those seeking flexibility.

data.title: Man Behind the XRP Lawsuit Could Get a White House AI Role Soon
data.description:
President Trump is weighing Jay Clayton, the former SEC chairman who sued Ripple, for the role of White House AI czar.

That possibility has unsettled parts of the crypto community, which is still watching Clayton’s regulatory legacy closely.

What Do Reports Say About Clayton as AI Czar?

CNN reported that Trump is actively seeking to fill the AI czar position within days. Clayton currently serves as Director of National Intelligence, overseeing the 18-agency intelligence community.

Asked about the role, Trump called Clayton “a good man” and said having him take it “is a good idea.”

Clayton signaled his approach to AI oversight during his July confirmation hearing for the intelligence post. He argued that AI requires careful handling because it represents both opportunity and risk.

Former AI czar David Sacks left the position in March. His government employee status had expired, leaving the role vacant for months while Trump searched for a replacement.

No formal timeline for naming a successor has been announced publicly.

Why Does Clayton’s Ripple Lawsuit Still Matter?

Clayton led the SEC when it sued Ripple in December 2020. The agency alleged Ripple raised $1.3 billion through unregistered securities sales dating back to 2013.

A judge later found that $728.9 million in direct institutional sales qualified as unregistered offerings.

Other XRP sales, including programmatic trading, fell outside that classification.

The case closed in August 2025 with a $125 million penalty. That figure sat well under the roughly $2 billion the SEC originally sought from Ripple.

A permanent injunction still restricts how Ripple sells XRP to US institutions, even though the litigation has ended.

The lawsuit also triggered a two-and-a-half-year delisting from major exchanges. It later delayed XRP’s path to spot ETFs until November 2025, well after Bitcoin and Ethereum had already captured that institutional demand.

Crypto advocates fear Clayton could bring that same strict posture to his next role with AI regulation. Whether that caution extends to AI policy is unclear right now. No evidence suggests crypto rules would tighten under his watch.

data.title: Crypto job postings more than triple to 1,241 in September as applications slide
data.description:
Crypto companies are hiring again. Job seekers, it seems, did not get the memo.

Monthly job postings on CryptoJobsList climbed from 382 in July to 1,241 in September, according to the platform's Q3 2026 hiring trends report. That September total marks the highest monthly posting volume of 2026.

Applications went the other direction. They fell from 26,728 in July to 19,605 in September, a decline of approximately 27% over the same stretch in which postings rose more than 220%.

CryptoJobsList, a hiring platform focused on Web3 and blockchain roles, broke the third quarter into three monthly snapshots.

July: 107 companies were actively hiring. Together they posted 382 jobs and received 26,728 applications.

August: The number of hiring companies dropped to 73. Yet job posts more than doubled to 886, while applications slipped to 24,641.

September: Active hiring companies jumped to 125. Job posts reached 1,241, and applications sank to 19,605.

The report characterizes the result as a tightening talent market.

Richard Botley, research and marketing lead at CryptoJobsList, described the quarter as a turning point. In his view, crypto firms are moving away from cost-cutting and toward more aggressive hiring.

Botley tied that shift to three forces: rising institutional interest in the sector, a wave of partnerships with traditional financial institutions, and renewed venture capital flowing into crypto companies.

According to the report, demand for specialized positions such as protocol developers, compliance leads, and quantitative traders appears to remain robust as the industry heads into Q4.

The report indicates the hiring rebound appears to be concentrated among larger companies rather than spread evenly across the sector.

The August figures hint at this dynamic. Fewer firms were hiring that month, yet total postings jumped, which suggests a smaller group of employers was doing much of the heavy lifting.

September broadened the picture somewhat, with active hiring companies climbing from 73 to 125. Still, the report's read is that the recovery is varied rather than universal.

For job seekers, the data points toward leverage. A market with more postings and fewer applications could lead to stronger compensation offers and better terms, particularly for the specialized roles the report highlights.

That potential upside is not evenly distributed, though. Candidates with protocol engineering, compliance, or quantitative trading backgrounds appear best positioned.

Several signals are worth watching into Q4. The first is whether September's posting volume holds or proves to be a seasonal peak. The second is whether applications stabilize. The third is whether hiring spreads beyond larger companies. Finally, if institutional interest, traditional finance partnerships, and venture capital inflows keep supporting the hiring push, the specialized roles in the report could remain in demand well into the new year.

data.title: The Insurance Industry Is Shedding Jobs. It's Not All About AI. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

After years of sharply rising premiums and fat profits, the insurance industry is at a crossroads. It's been shedding jobs-about 95,000 since early last year-as policy rates plateau for some, government subsidies dry up for others, and artificial intelligence threatens deeper cuts.

Insurance carriers and related services employed some 2.9 million workers as of September, according to new Labor Department data, marking a decline of around 3% since February 2025. The overall civilian labor force, on the other hand, has remained about the same size at about 170 million.

The industry's shrinkage makes it the biggest job shedder by category during that period. (Employment services, including temporary help, is a close second, falling by around 2.8%, or just under 90,000 jobs.)

The AI Scapegoat

AI could wipe out even more roles as it automates everything from processing simple claims, such as a broken car windshield, to generating instant quotes for new policies. But it's not the whole story.

Blaming AI for the cuts is "an overly simplistic explanation," says Robert Hartwig, a professor and Director of the Risk and Uncertainty Management Center at the University of South Carolina's Darla Moore School of Business.

"The reality is actually something far more basic," Hartwig tells Barron's.

Insurance Market Softening

A big reason for the job losses at property and casualty insurers such as State Farm, Progressive, and Farmers is that the firms are entering a softer part of their market cycle. "Rates are flattening and growth is slowing," says Hartwig. "In some cases those rates are actually declining," he adds.

Policy rates have risen so fast in recent years that such increases are no longer sustainable. What's more, higher financing costs and slowing population growth are lowering demand for new home insurance, Hartwig said.

The softer market is likely to drag on for a while. "We expect insurance labor force weakness to continue for a minimum of six months," says Michel Léonard, chief economist and data scientist at the Insurance Information Institute trade group.

Government Cuts to Medicaid and More

Health insurers are dealing with a different problem: cuts to government-subsidized Medicaid and Marketplace plans that have been enacted since President Donald Trump began his second term last year. Most recently, Elevance (formerly Anthem) filed notices in July and September with agencies in Washington, D.C., and Louisiana, respectively, for more than 300 job eliminations due to the insurer exiting its Medicaid-managed care contracts there.

Several other insurers, including Humana, Centene, and Cigna, have eliminated thousands of jobs this year, according to multiple media reports, to cut costs. None of the companies responded to Barron's request for comment on the cuts.

Shrinking profits, measured by an industry term known as the medical loss ratio (MLR), are another reason for head count cuts at health insurance companies. MLR refers to the share of premiums that insurers pay back in claims. Higher ratios equal lower profits, and those ratios have been rising along-with higher claims costs. As an example, Humana's MLR in the most recent quarter ending in July was 91.1%, up from 88.4% in the previous fiscal year.

While all this may sound like bad news for the industry, it hasn't hurt stock prices-at least not yet. For example, Humana share prices have risen more than 50% this year, in part because of aggressive cost-cutting measures, including layoffs, that have assured investors that insurers are well-positioned to weather the challenges ahead.

data.title: Africa's Richest Man Wants to Turn a Pristine Coastline Into an Oil Hub — WSJ
data.description:
By Caroline Kimeu in Lamu, Kenya and Alexandra Wexler in Johannesburg | Photography by Edwin Ndeke for WSJ

For seven centuries, the low-slung shoreline of Lamu Old Town, set against the turquoise waters of Kenya's coast, has attracted traders and speculators alike.

But few have wanted to stamp their imprint on its mangrove-lined seaboard as definitively as Africa's richest man, Nigerian oil magnate Aliko Dangote.

The billionaire is laying the groundwork for a giant refinery across the bay from the 700-year-old Swahili trading port, which the United Nations has designated a global treasure on this pristine portion of Indian Ocean coast.

The plans set up a clash between Dangote and economically minded Kenyan officials who support the project and the jobs it promises, and tourism operators and environmentalists worried about the potential impact on Lamu and neighboring islands, as well as the character of a remote site that has proven remarkably resistant to change.

Dangote Industries has already started soil tests and is ordering equipment for the refinery, according to group vice president Devakumar V.G. Edwin. "We want to do it on a fast-track basis," he said.

In late September, a Kenyan court ordered a pause to construction after more than 100 Lamu residents sued alleging that the refinery threatened ancestral land where they had farmed and buried their families for generations.

Kenyan officials say the $15 billion project would boost Kenya's energy security and reduce East Africa's reliance on refined-fuel imports from the Gulf. It would also create 60,000 jobs across construction and operations, they say. The Kenyan government has acquired an equity stake in the project, which has strong political backing, bolstered by the fallout of the U.S.-Iran war on international energy markets.

The U.N. describes Lamu Old Town, designated as a World Heritage site, as "the oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement in East Africa." Its narrow, labyrinthine streets are lined with stone buildings that blend Swahili, Arabic, Persian, Indian and European building styles.

Merchants followed the trade winds south from Oman and elsewhere in the Arab Peninsula for hundreds of years, bringing to the African coast everything from silks and porcelain to brass and paper. They would return when the winds shifted, their traditional dhow sailboats carrying slaves, spices, mangrove poles, ivory and skins.

"People come here because it feels like it's at the edge of the world," said Jamil Mbarak, whose family owns the Banana House and Wellness Centre resort in Shela, the next settlement down the beach from Lamu Old Town.

The Kenyan government has already built a large container port on the mainland a few miles from Lamu Island, its lights and cranes visible from the rooftop of Banana House. Mbarak fears that view may soon be blemished by passing oil tankers, and the breeze could carry industrial odors from the refinery.

The port was constructed as the terminus of a planned $25 billion economic corridor, with roads, rail and an oil pipeline linking Lamu to landlocked South Sudan and Ethiopia.

Although the Chinese-built port opened in 2021, progress on the rest of the corridor slowed due to funding deficits and attacks on construction workers by the Somalia-based Islamist extremist group al-Shabaab. The port itself remained largely unused.

But recently, stacks of Gulf-bound cargo have filled the previously empty container yard, diverted to Kenya by disruptions the Iran war has created in the Strait of Hormuz. In the first six months of this year, Lamu port handled double the cargo volumes it did in all of 2025, according to manager Abdulaziz Mzee. Kenyan officials see the refinery as a ticket to reviving the port and wider economic corridor, and some locals anticipate an infusion of resources into a corner of Kenya that has missed out on the economic growth enjoyed by Nairobi and the port of Mombasa, further down the coast.

Dangote Industries says it will import most of the crude oil it plans to refine from Nigeria, the U.S., Brazil, Libya, Angola and Ghana and to export refined products from Lamu's existing port, which the company says it will expand.

Dangote's move follows the success of his $20 billion refinery outside of Lagos, Nigeria, which reached full capacity in February-just in time to supply the world with diesel, jet fuel and gasoline that doesn't need to pass through the Strait of Hormuz or the narrow Bab al-Mandeb waterway on the southwestern corner of the Arab Peninsula. Dangote plans to double the capacity of the Nigerian refinery to 1.4 million barrels a day. In September, his company began selling shares in the facility, aiming to raise $1.6 billion from up to 10 million shareholders.

The company projects its Lamu refinery will process 700,000 barrels of crude oil a day.

Monicah Muthoni Marubu, a Kenyan lawmaker from Lamu County, said that while the island's heritage status should be protected, it makes up only a fraction of a larger county.

"We love the tourism industry-it's a major contributor to our economy," said Marubu. But, she said, tourism isn't sufficient to keep most people employed.

"Our culture is beautiful, but we cannot eat culture," she said.

Dangote Industries promises to adhere to stringent European Union and U.S. oil-quality and environmental standards, to ensure it can sell to either market, and says it has applied for environmental certifications.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, which designates World Heritage sites, says it has asked the Kenyan government for information about the Lamu refinery plans. But the agency hasn't taken a position on the development.

Unesco "has consistently considered extractive-industry activities to be incompatible with World Heritage status," an agency spokeswoman said. "While a refinery project does not in itself constitute an extractive-industry activity, as with any major development project, its compatibility with the protection of a World Heritage property would need to be assessed on the basis of its potential impacts" on what the U.N. calls its "outstanding universal value."

Environmental and heritage studies would be needed before decisions over the refinery were reached, the spokeswoman said.

"This project threatens to damage one of East Africa's most-fragile ecosystems, while locking Kenya into a risky fossil-fuel future," said Sherelee Odayar, a campaigner with Greenpeace Africa.

"Decisions of this magnitude cannot bypass the people of Lamu."

Lamu hosts 70% of Kenya's mangrove forests that provide a massive carbon sink and are vital breeding grounds for marine life and migratory birds. Government studies have predicted that more than a third of those mangroves could be lost during development of the economic corridor. Locals say dredging for the port already damaged coral reefs, resulting in a decline in marine life and tourist interest at a popular snorkeling site.

Past developments, including the port and abandoned coal and wind-power plants, left farmers and fishermen in yearslong battles over compensation and resettlement.

Fishermen fear expanded industrial operations will restrict access to close-in fishing grounds, pushing them into riskier waters.

"It will affect us because big ships will be passing through so there will be more restrictions, and we would need to go much further to fish," said Omar Lali, a 27-year-old fisherman.

A big wild card for the project remains al-Shabaab, the al Qaeda affiliate that has expanded its war against the Somali government into border areas of Kenya.

U.S. and Kenyan troops engaged in the fight against al-Shabaab are stationed at Kenya's Manda Bay Naval base, a short distance from the Lamu port. In 2020, al-Shabaab fighters attacked the base, killing a U.S. soldier and two American contractors.

data.title: FlyDubai Attacker Used 'Crash Ax,' a Common Fixture on Many Jets — WSJ
data.description:
By Jon Gambrell, Benjamin Katz and Feliz Solomon

DUBAI-A central mystery of this week's attempted downing of FlyDubai Flight 1073 has been how the co-pilot managed to smuggle a weapon into the plane to carry out his attack. It turns out he didn't. The weapon he used is a cockpit fixture.

United Arab Emirates authorities said Saturday the co-pilot attacked his captain with the plane's crash ax-a tool that regulators around the world require airplanes to carry.

Designed for use as an emergency tool to tear through metal in case of a fire or a crash, the crash ax instead became a weapon the co-pilot wielded to wound his captain and try to damage the controls of the Boeing 737 MAX 8 over Saudi Arabia.

The use of the ax highlights the tough trade-offs regulators face as they try to guard against competing threats to safety on planes. Those include reinforced cockpit doors designed to keep out dangerous passengers like those behind the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks in the U.S., but which make it harder to stop internal threats like the FlyDubai incident this week.

The ax is required to be on board U.S. carriers as well as those in the U.A.E. But Wednesday's attack likely will draw renewed scrutiny to the risks it poses, particularly in situations where the danger lies in the flight deck.

"There's some sort of process in place for checking out who the pilots are, that clearly did not work, there was some failure there," said Chuck Freilich, a former deputy national security adviser in Israel. "In the end, there's a limit to what you can do. One lunatic or highly motivated Islamist, if they are willing to die, will always find loopholes in even the most effective security systems."

The use of the crash ax resolves one of the most pressing questions surrounding the attack on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv: how the co-pilot accessed a weapon and smuggled it aboard. Dubai International Airport implements strict security checks on passengers and crew alike, experts say.

Crash axes are stored on aircraft to be used in an emergency to either fight fires or cut through metal in a crash. In case of a blaze behind paneling, pilots train to use the ax to make a hole through which they can spray a fire extinguisher.

Though the ax is usually kept in a sheath at the back of the cockpit, pilots said the tool is readily accessible and possible to withdraw without another pilot noticing.

Typically, the tool resembles a short hatchet that has two sides-one is a traditional-looking blade and another that is a claw or pick able to tear away metal or a window.

A statement Saturday from U.A.E. attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said the co-pilot "began executing his plan during the flight, attacking the captain inside the flight deck using a crash ax and attempting to take control of the aircraft's flight controls."

Investigators are still trying to determine his motives, he said.

The statement didn't identify the co-pilot. The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that he is an Omani national named Hamam al-Hammami who had previously been banned from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views. The U.A.E. and FlyDubai declined to comment on the matter citing the continuing investigation.

Passengers seated near the front of the plane told the Journal that the men who secured Hammami said they didn't see the weapon, but word began spreading among them that it could have been an ax. Passengers said they were so focused on securing the attacker that no one looked for his weapon after the fact.

The crash ax typically remains hidden from passengers in flight. Some flights have an additional ax in the main cabin as well. European regulators require either a crash ax or a crowbar on aircraft registered there.

The crash ax's presence is an anomaly in an environment where passengers and crew are screened for blades before boarding and airports keep close track of knives in restaurants beyond the security check.

Pilots have recounted having everything from metal cutlery to selfie sticks confiscated at security have long regarded the ax as a bizarre exception in light of changes in aviation security following the Sept. 11 attacks.

"You can't bring nail clippers but there's this bad boy in the flight deck," a captain for a major European carrier said in a message with a photo of the ax. Boeing's website also lists them for sale.

The crash ax has been used in the past as a weapon of last resort by pilots in crises.

In November 1985, an EgyptAir pilot said he smashed an ax into one of the Palestinian militants who hijacked his flight during a chaotic Egyptian rescue attempt in Malta that left dozens dead. In 2000, an Alaska Airlines pilot defended his cockpit with the ax when a passenger broke in and tried to crash the flight.

After Sept. 11, the crash ax became both a defensive weapon and a worry. The U.S. Air Line Pilots Association told captains to be prepared to use the ax to kill an intruder. Others worried it could be another tool for hijackers, particularly if they breached the cockpit.

"If you close the [cockpit] door and seal it up like a bank vault, that becomes a problem," U.S. Transportation Secretary Norman Mineta said at the time.

That nearly became the case on the FlyDubai flight, which had the reinforced doors common on modern aircraft that require a pilot or a combination code to enter. The flight's captain, while bleeding from the attack, said he managed a desperate lunge to open the door, allowing passengers and a backup crew access to the cockpit with just moments to spare.

data.title: 'A hero of our times': Mankind Pharma to give Rs.1 crore to FlyDubai Capt Smit Machchhar
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- Mankind Pharma has announced Rs.1 crore contribution to Captain Smit Machchhar and his family, describing the gesture as an expression of gratitude for his courage and leadership during what the company called an "unimaginable crisis".

The pharmaceutical company announced it through a statement on LinkedIn. Along with the post, it also shared a letter from its Vice Chairman and Managing Director Rajeev Juneja, in which he praised Machchhar for putting his crew and passengers before himself.

"Some acts of courage stay with an entire nation," Mankind Pharma said. "In a moment of unimaginable crisis, #CaptSmitMachchhar showed composure and responsibility, and put his crew and every passenger before himself."

The company said the contribution was its "humble expression of gratitude" and added, "Capt. Smit, you have made India proud. We salute you."

Juneja, while reposting Mankind Pharma's statement, wrote that the company believed that pride and appreciation should translate into meaningful action.

"When we witness an act of extraordinary courage and our hearts are filled with pride, we have a choice: let that emotion pass with time, or turn it into meaningful action," Juneja said.

He said the company decided to support Machchhar after seeing news about his actions, adding that Mankind wanted to go beyond praising his courage and "stand behind our words with meaningful action".

"Because emotions fade, but actions leave a lasting impact," Juneja said.

According to Juneja, the Rs.1 crore contribution is Mankind Pharma's way of conveying that it recognises Machchhar's courage and stands with him and his family.

In the letter addressed to Machchhar, Juneja described him as "a hero of our times" and said his courage, composure and sense of responsibility had touched people in India and around the world.

Juneja said Machchhar demonstrated leadership at a time when fear and pressure were high and the lives of passengers and crew depended on his decisions.

"A leader is not tested when everything is going well. The real test comes in a moment of extreme crisis, when fear is natural, pressure is immense, and the lives of so many people depend on your decisions," he wrote.

He said Machchhar had thought about his crew and passengers and taken responsibility for the lives entrusted to him.

"No amount of money can ever equal the value of the lives you protected or the inspiration you have given to millions," Juneja wrote, describing the Rs.1 crore contribution as a "small expression" of the company's respect, gratitude and admiration.

He concluded the letter by thanking Machchhar for putting others before himself and for "reminding all of us that, even in the most difficult moments, humanity must always come first".

Machchhar was reportedly stabbed with a knife by his co-pilot on the FlyDubai flight from UAE to Israel on Wednesday in an apparent act of hijack. Despite being seriously injured, Machchhar was able to open the cockpit door by activating the door release. This allowed the crew members and passengers to enter the cockpit and overpower the attacker.

The flight carrying 174 passengers was later diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi also had a telephonic conversation with Machchhar on Friday. PM Modi praised his courage and presence of mind during the incident.

data.title: Mumbai airport Terminal 1 revamp: 91% passenger traffic to remain unaffected
data.description:
Ninety-one per cent of the city’s passenger traffic will remain unaffected as Mumbai International Airport Limited undertakes partial redevelopment of Terminal 1 from January 2027, Adani Airports Holdings Limited (AAHL) chief executive officer Arun Bansal said in a statement on Saturday evening.

“Ninety-one per cent of Mumbai airport’s passenger traffic will remain unaffected even as we undertake redevelopment of the age-old infrastructure that was in urgent need of repairs. Only the north section of Terminal 1B, which accounts for around one-third of Terminal 1’s capacity, is being demolished in Phase 1 to minimise passenger inconvenience and operational disruption. The transition to Navi Mumbai Airport is temporary and does not represent a permanent shift of Mumbai Airport traffic,” Bansal said.

Airlines offered temporary relocation

To ensure continuity of operations and minimise inconvenience to passengers, the Adani group has provided airlines with the option to temporarily relocate their operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport at their discretion.

“ AAHL will support airlines through this transition and will provide all necessary assistance to ensure a smooth and seamless migration of services,” it said

Airlines resist proposed shift

The airport operator has proposed that one-third of international flights shift to Navi Mumbai from October 26, but airlines are resisting the plan, calling it a forced relocation.

data.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
data.description:
By Jana Winter, Raphael Satter and AJ Vicens

A key member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which claims to have stolen data on every FBI employee, was detained this week in Jordan, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. Two of the sources said he was cooperating with the FBI to identify his fellow hackers.

Saif al-Din Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities, the three sources said. Two of them said he was brought into custody on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the circumstances of Khader’s detention or his current whereabouts. Two sources said that he is helping the FBI and global law enforcement locate the other hackers in the group.

The FBI declined to comment on any specific arrest or activity abroad but said that the bureau "continues to aggressively investigate the recent cyber incident allegedly involving ShinyHunters, having already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects — and we will spare no resource in bringing each of the responsible individuals to justice."

Reuters’ attempts to reach Khader and members of his family over the past week and a half have been unsuccessful.

The detention of Khader — whose alleged hacker nickname is Rey — is the latest twist in the case of ShinyHunters, a motley crew believed by experts to consist mainly of young, English-speaking hackers focused on data theft and extortion.

Their theft of what they claim are mountains of data on every single FBI employee has drawn comparisons to the allegedly Chinese-linked intrusion at the US Office of Personnel Management in 2015, which compromised sensitive details on millions of Americans who had been vetted for security clearances.

data.title: Dr Reddy’s US arm faces $32,350 IRS penalty over fiscal year misclassification
data.description:
Dr Reddy’s Laboratories said its step-down wholly owned subsidiary, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, Inc. (DRL Inc), has received a penalty of $32,350.20 from the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) over misclassification of the fiscal year reference at the time of tax payment.

DRL Inc received the final transcript dated September 25, 2026, from the US Department of the Treasury, Internal Revenue Service, Cincinnati, Ohio, on October 2, 2026.

According to the company, the penalty relates to the misclassification of the fiscal year reference at the time of tax payment.

Dr Reddy’s said that, based on its evaluation, there is no material impact on the company’s financials, operations or other activities.

Earlier on Sep 11, in a separate development, drugmaker had said the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) completed a records assessment at its active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility in Mexico, with two observations issued at the conclusion of the assessment.

The assessment was conducted under Section 704(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act at Industrias Químicas Falcón de México, S.A. de C.V., also known as Dr Reddy’s Mexico, located in Jiutepec, Morelos, Mexico.

The records assessment was conducted from July 17 to September 8, 2026. At the conclusion of the assessment, the USFDA issued Form FDA 2953 containing two observations. Dr Reddy’s said it will respond to the observations within the stipulated timeline.

Dr Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd shares closed 2.51% lower at ₹1,202 on October 1, 2026, at NSE.

data.title: Worldcoin Rallies As World Chain's Total Value Locked Climbs As Bitcoin Slides Below $85K
data.description:
Key points:
  • Worldcoin rose over 7% on Saturday, extending a run that has it up roughly 23% over seven days and 61% over a month.
  • Total value locked on World Chain, the layer-2 network run by the same project, climbed 12.28% over 24 hours, according to DefiLlama data.
  • The move comes as President Greg Brockman signed for OpenAI instead of CEO Sam Altman, chairman of Tools for Humanity, which makes Worldcoin. 

Worldcoin (WLD) edged higher on Saturday, outpacing Bitcoin (BTC) on daily gains as activity on its own blockchain picked up alongside it, as the apex cryptocurrency traded below $85,000.

Total value locked (TVL) on World Chain, which is the Ethereum (ETH) layer-2 network run by the same project behind the WLD token, rose 12.28% over 24 hours to $45.12 million, according to DefiLlama data.

The token's move extended a longer run, and WLD was up roughly 23% over seven days, 61% over a month, and 25.2% so far this year, or year-to-date (YTD). That run came against a weaker market, where crypto market capitalization fell over 2%, with Bitcoin, the apex cryptocurrency, dominating at 57.7%.

Worldcoin was one of the top-trending tickers on Stocktwits. WLD’s price was up over 7% during the past 24 hours.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around WLD improved to ‘extremely bullish’ zone from the 'bullish' zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Bets Against WLD Burned

Worldcoin's rise in price caught traders who had bet against it. A liquidation happens when a trader borrows to make a leveraged bet, the price moves the wrong way, and the exchange closes the position automatically to stop the losses from growing.

Over the past hour, WLD positions worth about $241,590 were wiped out, against about $133,050 on Bitcoin, according to CoinGlass data. The Worldcoin figure was roughly 82% higher, even though Bitcoin’s market cap is significantly larger.

Most of that hour's damage fell on short positions, which are bets that a price will fall. CoinGlass put the hour's total across all tokens at $1.94 million, of which $1.14 million came from shorts.

The longer view was the reverse. Over 24 hours, $343.96 million was liquidated, and $305.45 million of that came from long positions, which are bets that a price will rise. That fits a market where most tokens fell, and Worldcoin was the exception.

Worldcoin's AI Link Draws Attention

WLD trades as an AI-adjacent token, so sentiment around the sector tends to reach it. Worldcoin and its creator, Tools for Humanity, are different firms, but they’re linked via their chairman, Sam Altman, the CEO of the AI company, OpenAI (OPEAZZX).

The rally comes on the heels on six executives signed a voluntary AI safety commitment at the White House on Sept. 29, among them Google's (GOOG) Sundar Pichai, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Meta's (META) Mark Zuckerberg, xAI's Elon Musk, and Nvidia's (NVDA) Jensen Huang.

OpenAI president Greg Brockman signed for his company rather than chief executive Sam Altman, who is chairman of Tools for Humanity, the company behind Worldcoin.

However, on Friday Altman said Cerebras (CRBS) is also a “close partner” of OpenAI, who stated the businesses had a “deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed.” The transaction includes OpenAI’s agreement to use 750 megawatts of Cerebras computing capacity through 2028, with Cerebras stating the arrangement is worth over $20 billion.

data.title: Eni and Repsol said to be weighing a partial sale of top Venezuela gas field
data.description:
European energy groups Eni and Repsol are considering whether to sell a portion of their stakes in the Perla natural gas field off Venezuela’s coast, Bloomberg reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The companies that currently own 50% each of the venture are seeking additional funds to help develop the massive offshore field, which they discovered in 2009 in the shallow waters close to Venezuela’s border with Colombia.

Eni and Repsol are seeking a partial sale, the people said, asking for anonymity, as they are not authorized to discuss confidential information. Eni and Repsol didn’t respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment.

Perla is estimated to hold approximately 17T cubic feet of gas, making it one of the largest gas fields in Latin America.

In April, the companies reached a deal with the Venezuelan government to begin natural gas exports from the oil-rich nation by the end of 2031. The agreement with the country’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, will enable the duo to more than double production at the Perla field.

data.title: Real estate stocks feel the pain as borrowing costs climb
data.description:
Mortgage rates rising to a three-year high dominated the real estate sector last week, as 30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.28% as of Oct. 1. With elevated interest rates, the Mortgage Bankers Association's Composite Index, a measure of the mortgage demand, continued to swoon.

Even early in the week, climbing Treasury yields pushed down housing and mortgage stocks. They didn't fare any better for the rest of the week.

The State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR slipped 1.5% during the week ended Oct. 2, a deeper loss than the S&P 500’s 0.3% decline. By sector, health REITs performed the best, rising 0.6%. Office REITs suffered the most, dropping 4.7%.

The stocks that dropped the most included Fermi , the energy-focused REIT that supports AI development, which sank 11% during the week, and mortgage REIT Annaly Capital Management , which dove 10%.

Real estate stocks that rose the most included Bill Ackman's Howard Hughes Holdings , which gained 3.8%, and OutFront Media , which also increased 3.8%.

Other real estate news from the week:

  • Apollo Commercial Real Estate stockholders approved the company’s dissolution.

  • Activist Irenic plans to vote against Independence Realty’s $8.1B purchase of Centerspace .

  • Brixmor Property and Everview Partners agreed to acquire Slate Grocery REIT (SGR.UN:CA) for $2.34B.

  • National Healthcare Properties agreed to sell 40 outpatient medical facilities for ~$531M and plans to use the proceeds to help repay debt and fund senior housing operating portfolio acquisitions.

  • The FHFA house price index  and the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Index showed that home prices rose more than expected in July, but the year-over-year increase lagged inflation growth.

data.title: Vedanta Power Q2 sales rise 26% to 5,593 MU on stronger plant performance
data.description:
Vedanta Power Ltd on Saturday said that its power sales rose by 26 per cent to 5,593 million units (MU) in the second quarter of the current fiscal.

The company’s power sales stood at 4,433 MU in the second quarter of the previous fiscal.

The company recorded 10,817 million units of power sales in the first half of the current fiscal, registering a 32 per cent Y-o-Y growth, as stronger plant performance and improved availability across its portfolio drove robust momentum, Vedanta Power said in a statement.

Meenakshi Energy drives growth

The growth was driven by a sharp increase in generation at Meenakshi Energy and a turnaround at Jharsuguda Thermal Plant.

At Meenakshi Energy, power sales increased 111 per cent Y-o-Y to 1,470 million units in Q2, taking the overall sales in the first half of the fiscal year to 2,820 million units, up 160 per cent Y-o-Y.

The performance reflects operations of the expanded 1,000-MW capacity base, strengthening the plant’s contribution to the company’s overall generation portfolio.

Jharsuguda plant turnaround

The momentum was further supported by a turnaround at the Jharsuguda Thermal Plant, where power sales rose 186 per cent year-on-year to 873 million units in the September quarter.

Sales during the first half increased 59 per cent to 1,559 million units. The plant’s availability also improved sharply, with the plant availability factor rising to 98 per cent in the quarter from 43 per cent in the year-ago period, aiding higher generation and sales.

Focus on reliable power

Alongside these growth drivers, the Talwandi Sabo Thermal Plant continued to provide a strong and consistent operating base for the portfolio.

The company remains focused on delivering reliable power while supporting India’s growing and evolving energy requirements.

Shares of Vedanta Power were listed on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in June. The listing ceremony, on June 15, was led by Vedanta Group Chairman Anil Agarwal.
